reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about diffusion kinetics, kinetic trapping, and phase selection in noble metal HEA nanoparticles, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge covers general diffusion principles, but the application to this specific material system and synthesis regime requires supporting citations, which are absent.
premises: Rapid heating/cooling limits atomic diffusion, causing kinetic trapping of non-equilibrium configurations
Slower thermal ramps allow sufficient diffusion to approach thermodynamic equilibrium
Kinetic trapping leads to phase separation, elemental segregation, and irregular morphology
Enhanced diffusion promotes uniform single-phase solid-solution formation
The mechanism applies to noble metal–based HEA nanoparticles with >5 elements
